scope: Second real-660 forward test of the repair-shadow-motion-lag skill
summary: The evolved motion-lag skill passes its scoped 2-D acceptance contract: median-filtered arm centroids, continuous motion confidence, and low-alpha-only camera-frame warping align shadow cleanup on 149 high-motion frames without breaking temporal or protection gates.
evidence: The independent assessment SHA-256 is 17e0a4c1820bfeade2d67e316884ebe8899df9a2c52d18f22af401a98239d283 and all seven automatic/human gates pass.
Motion alignment activates on 149 frames with maximum capped camera-frame displacement 28.2860 pixels.
Relative to accepted v71, ROI jerk changes from 1.6804897 to 1.6858711, ratio 1.00320 within the 1.03 non-regression gate.
Protected robot/flower content and pixels outside the safety mask are exact in every preencode frame.

All 149 high-motion frames plus the 24 largest-displacement frames were reviewed with v71/candidate/difference sheets; no leading/trailing halo, exposed source skin, migrated robot material, or flower edit was found.
lessons: Continuous confidence and centroid denoising remove the jerk regression caused by a hard motion threshold.
Warp only low-alpha shadow support and preserve alpha at or above 0.70 in place.
An independent assessment can promote a renderer run whose immutable manifest correctly retains its original pending-review state.
limitations: WORKING is scoped to the accepted 660-frame H3 2-D composite and its pinned masks, not arbitrary scenes or physical illumination.
High-motion clean-plate distance is a proxy and was allowed 3% non-regression; perceptual attachment still required manual review.
The skill does not generate physical contact shadows or infer 3-D lighting.
next_actions: Use this reviewed motion candidate as the parent for bounded shadow-intensity lightening.
Keep the rejected hard-threshold run available as a regression fixture.
